ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a logic block marked “=1” and with a small inversion circle at the output terminal. It has two inputs: the lower input is A, and the upper input comes from the feedback line of the output Q of the flip-flop on the right. Therefore, this logic block is equivalent to an XNOR/equality judgment circuit that compares whether A and Q are equal. The output of this logic block is connected to the J and K inputs of the JK flip-flop on the right; the flip-flop on the right is acted on by the CP clock, the output terminal is Q, and Q is also fed back to the logic block on the left. Reasoning: Discuss according to the relationship between the current Q and A in two cases. If the current Q=A, then the XNOR output is 1, so J=K=1; under the action of the next CP, the JK flip-flop toggles, and Q becomes the inverse value of the original, therefore becoming Q≠A. If the current Q≠A, then the XNOR output is 0, so J=K=0; under the action of the next CP, the JK flip-flop holds the original state, and Q still is not equal to A. From this it can be known that, under the regulating action of CP, the circuit will make Q remain as the inverted signal of A. Therefore, when A inputs a rectangular wave, Q outputs a rectangular wave opposite to the waveform of A.

If Q is already unequal to A, the XNOR output is 0, so J=K=0 and the next CP pulse keeps Q unchanged. Therefore after CP action Q is maintained as the complement of A; for rectangular-wave A, Q is a rectangular wave opposite in phase/level to A.
